questions.prompt: What is the capital city of El Salvador?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the El Salvador article.

questions.proof: To the south by the Pacific Ocean and its capital and largest city is San Salvador.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with El Salvador?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture El Salvador on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the El Salvador article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1546, Carlos I from _____ named San Salvador a city.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “named”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the El Salvador article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1546, Carlos I from Spain named San Salvador a city.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was in the top 3 in Central America (behind Costa Rica and _____).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Rica”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the El Salvador article, under the heading “Background”.

questions.proof: It was in the top 3 in Central America (behind Costa Rica and Panama).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The highest point in El Salvador is Cerro El Pital, at 2,730 metres (8,957 ft), on the border with _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the El Salvador article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The highest point in El Salvador is Cerro El Pital, at 2,730 metres (8,957 ft), on the border with Honduras.
